Run A Plastic-Free Picnic

Everyone brings food with zero single-use plastic. Harder than it sounds, and you'll learn a lot about what you buy.

Cost
Under £20pp
Time
Half-day
People
Small Group (3-6), Large Group (7+)
Where
Park / Outdoor
Bring
Reusable containers and cutlery

Why this matters

Most household plastic use is invisible until you try to avoid it - it turns out to be nearly everything, and that realisation changes shopping habits more effectively than any amount of general advice. Doing it as a challenge with friends makes the learning concrete and shared, rather than an individual exercise in guilt.

How to do it

Everyone brings a dish to a picnic, with one rule: no single-use plastic anywhere. Not in the packaging you bought it in, not in how you transport it, not in the cutlery.

You'll immediately discover this is much harder than expected. That's the point.

What tends to work: - Buy loose fruit and vegetables, and bring your own bags - Bakery bread in paper, or bake it - Cheese and meat from a counter into your own container - most will do this if you ask, though some will refuse - Glass jars, beeswax wraps, tins and reusable containers for transport - Proper cutlery and cloth napkins from home - Drinks in glass, cans or a big refillable container rather than individual bottles

Make it a challenge rather than a rule. Compare notes on what was impossible, where you had to compromise, and which shops made it easy. The conversation is more valuable than the picnic.

Things people usually learn: that "recyclable" plastic often isn't recycled in practice, that most bulk stores are cheaper than expected, that the biggest offenders are snacks and anything pre-prepared, and that asking a butcher or deli to use your container is far less awkward than anticipated.

Take everything home. A plastic-free picnic that leaves anything behind has rather missed the point.
